answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the wharf check immediately, the spiral audit keeps the resolved set and the marble replay makes public exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 82 aliases as a result burns the reading cost 82 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
